items.title: Take a short walk after meals
items.text: In real adults (CGMacros), a walk after a meal went with a rise only about 3.2 mg/dL smaller (95% CI -6.9 to 0.5): not distinguishable from zero. Your sugar rose about 11.1 mg/dL less after meals when you walked. Aim for 10 to 20 minutes after dinner, where the synthetic program saw the biggest gain (18.3 mg/dL). If you take insulin or a sulfonylurea (glipizide, glyburide, glimepiride), ask your care team about low sugar before adding walks after meals.

rejected.text: Aim for a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner to help with your sugar levels. Walking after meals went with a rise in sugar about 3.2 mg/dL smaller and your sugar rose about 11.1 mg/dL less after meals when you walked.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Try to avoid eating dinner at 8 pm or later, as sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners. None of your 12 scored dinners started at 8 pm or later, so keep it that way.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You averaged 13.0 hours of overnight fast, and 42.9% of nights reached 13 hours, which is a good habit to continue. In the program, adding the overnight fast to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points compared with coaching alone.
